title: Release
description: The body of the signed POST /v1/dispatches/<dispatch_id>/release, application/json: the starter gives the run back, why, and whether the run should wait for another claim. Before the handover, a release with retry: true returns the same run, with the same run_id, to the queue, as a lapsed lease does. After the handover, while the run goes on, a release ends the run, since a dispatch whose handover is answered never goes back to the queue: the release is answered as a success, the signed 204, not 409, and the gateway refuses the run's key with 410 when the job attaches. With retry: true it then queues a new run, with a new run_id and a new run key, since a run key is handed over at most once per run. A dispatch_id that is unknown, or of another node pool than the key's, is refused 403 forbidden, with the same signed body either way, so nobody learns whether an id exists; the control plane decides this before any 409 or 410. The signature with the pool's access key and that check authorise the request, not the id. A release after the dispatch ended is refused, 410 gone, as refusal.schema.json describes; so is a release after the run's end, since the dispatch ends with its run. On success the control plane answers a signed 204 with no body. It is signed with the pool's access key as definitions.schema.json describes. The control plane refuses a time more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, or a request whose signature it has already seen, with an unsigned 401. A member this schema does not define is refused, invalid_request.

version.description: The document format. The control plane refuses a version it does not read.

time.description: When the starter built the body, RFC 3339 in UTC with whole seconds. The control plane refuses a time more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, with an unsigned 401.

reason.description: Why the starter gives the run back, display text, 1 to 200 characters.

retry.description: true when the run should wait for another claim: before the handover the same run waits again; after it, a new run, with a new run_id and a new run key. false when it should not.
